skill.name: asana-automation
skill.description: Automate Asana tasks, projects, sections, teams, and workspace queries through Composio's Rube MCP tools.
skill.summary: Manage Asana work through guided Rube MCP tool sequences.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 46 shell alerts and 13 reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and ordinary Asana documentation. Real risks remain from third-party MCP access and non-transactional parallel changes.

remediation.issue: Rube MCP receives delegated access to the user's Asana account.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the intermediary, requested OAuth scopes, data handling, and revocation process before connection.

remediation.issue: Parallel requests can leave partial changes when individual actions fail.
remediation.suggestion: Preview every action, require confirmation, limit batch size, and report each result for recovery.

- `projects`: Array of project GIDs to add task to
1. `ASANA_SUBMIT_PARALLEL_REQUESTS` - Execute multiple API calls in parallel [Required]
- `actions`: Array of action objects with method, path, and data
- Asana uses cursor-based pagination with `offset` parameter
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Each action must be a valid Asana API call

content.user_title: Automate Asana Workflows with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Manual Asana updates make recurring project work slow and inconsistent. This skill guides reliable task, project, section, team, and workspace operations through Rube MCP.
actual_capabilities: Search current Rube MCP tool schemas before selecting an Asana action.
Resolve workspace and project names to Asana GIDs.
Search, list, create, and inspect tasks and subtasks.
Create projects and sections, then assign tasks to sections.
List Asana teams, team members, workspace users, and the current user.
Submit parallel Asana API actions and continue cursor-based pagination.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active OAuth connection to Asana.
Available actions depend on current Rube schemas and the connected account permissions.
Successful parallel actions are not rolled back when another action fails.
The documented workflows do not cover comments, attachments, portfolios, rules, or task deletion.

use_cases.title: Create Structured Project Work
use_cases.description: Create tasks and subtasks with project placement, assignees, notes, and due dates.

use_cases.title: Organize Delivery Boards
use_cases.description: Create sections and move tasks into the correct project stage.

use_cases.title: Audit Workspace Activity
use_cases.description: List projects, tasks, teams, and users across an authorized workspace.

prompt_templates.title: List My Workspaces
prompt_templates.prompt: Find my available Asana workspaces. Show each workspace name and GID without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Project Task
prompt_templates.prompt: In [workspace], create a task named [task] in [project]. Assign [person], set [date], and confirm details before creation.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Project Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: In [workspace], create project [project] with sections [sections]. Preview the planned structure and request confirmation before each write.
prompt_templates.scenario: Set up a new delivery workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare parallel Asana actions for [goal]. Resolve all GIDs, validate each action, limit the batch to [count], and request confirmation before execution.

output_examples.input: List projects in the Product workspace.
Create a task for the launch checklist, due Friday.
output_examples.output: Prepared task: Launch checklist. Project: Release Plan. Due date: 2026-07-24. Awaiting confirmation before creation.

output_examples.input: Move three approved tasks into the In Review section.
output_examples.output: Moved 3 tasks to In Review. Each action succeeded, and the affected task names are listed in the result.

best_practices: Call RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS first and follow the current schema.
Resolve workspace, project, task, section, and team GIDs before write operations.
Preview writes and require confirmation, especially for parallel requests.
anti_patterns: Do not guess GIDs from names or previous workspaces.
Do not send large parallel batches without limits and per-action validation.
Do not assume failed parallel actions roll back successful changes.

faq.question: What connection does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Rube MCP and an active Asana OAuth connection.

faq.question: Does the skill need an Asana API key?
faq.answer: The documented setup uses OAuth through Rube MCP instead of a manually entered API key.

faq.question: Can it create tasks and subtasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents task creation, subtask creation, project placement, assignment, notes, and due dates.

faq.question: Can it manage projects and sections?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create projects and sections, list them, and add tasks to sections.

faq.question: How does it handle pagination?
faq.answer: It checks next_page and passes the returned offset into the next request.

faq.question: Are parallel operations transactional?
faq.answer: No. A failed action does not roll back successful actions, so review and limit each batch.
